FAQ

Questions, answered

Contact us →
See all FAQs →
How do I open an account with you?

Click "Open Free Demat Account" at the top of the page to apply online on Mirae Asset Sharekhan's secure portal, with Fin Venue Ventures as your Authorised Person. Keep your PAN, Aadhaar-linked mobile and bank details ready. If you need help, call us and our team will guide you.

Where are my shares held?

Your shares are held in your own demat account with a SEBI-registered depository, and trades are executed through Mirae Asset Sharekhan on NSE and BSE.

Is the portfolio review really free?

Yes. The consultation and portfolio review are complimentary and carry no obligation to invest.

What is Investiger?

Investiger is our in-house mini-PMS, actively handled by a dedicated fund manager, with a lower entry point than a traditional PMS.

Do you work with NRIs?

Yes. We work with NRIs as well as resident investors. Contact us and we will explain the right account type and documents for you.

When can I reach you?

Our office in Malad West, Mumbai is open Monday to Saturday, 8:30 AM to 6:30 PM. Call +91 93244 99656, or email info@finvenueventures.com.

Who we are

An Authorised Person of Mirae Asset Sharekhan, led by a Chartered Accountant and built around personal guidance.

Who we are

Your partner in building wealth

Fin Venue Ventures Private Limited is an Authorised Person of Mirae Asset Sharekhan, helping individuals and families invest with clarity and confidence.

From your first equity trade to a diversified portfolio across mutual funds, bonds and unlisted opportunities, we combine Mirae Asset Sharekhan's research and execution strength with hands-on, personal guidance, so every decision is backed by data, not guesswork.

Our mission

To make expert-grade investing accessible to every Indian household, delivered with transparency, discipline and genuine personal care at every step.

Who we serve

Built for every kind of investor

  • First-time investors
  • Business owners & entrepreneurs
  • Working professionals
  • Retirees & senior citizens
  • NRIs
  • HNI & ultra-HNI families
What we stand for

      Risk disclosure on derivatives (F&O)

      • 9 out of 10 individual traders in equity Futures and Options Segment incurred net losses.
      • On an average, loss makers registered net trading loss close to ₹50,000.
      • Over and above the net trading losses incurred, loss makers expended an additional 28% of net trading losses as transaction costs.

      Source: SEBI study dated January 25, 2023 on "Analysis of Profit and Loss of Individual Traders dealing in equity Futures and Options (F&O) Segment", wherein aggregate level findings are based on annual profit/loss incurred by individual traders in equity F&O during FY 2021-22.

      About this charter

      Fin Venue Ventures Private Limited is an Authorised Person of Mirae Asset Sharekhan Ltd., a SEBI-registered stock broker. As per SEBI, every stock broker publishes an Investor Charter that sets out the services you can expect, your rights and responsibilities, and how complaints are handled. This page summarises it in plain language. Your broker's complete charter is available on sharekhan.com ↗.

      Vision and mission

      Vision: to uphold the highest standards of ethics and compliance while helping clients trade in securities in a fair and transparent manner, and to contribute to building wealth for investors.

      • Provide high-quality, dependable service through innovation and technology.
      • Build relationships with investors based on trust.
      • Maintain the highest standards of compliance.
      • Put investor protection first in everything we do.

      Services provided to investors

      • Execution of trades on your behalf on NSE and BSE.
      • Issue of a contract note for every trade within 24 hours of execution.
      • Timely issue of margin requirements and other alerts.
      • Pay-out of funds and securities, and settlement of your running account as per your chosen preference.
      • Regular statements of funds and securities.
      • Risk management systems to protect you against excessive losses.
      • Resolution of your complaints within the timelines below.

      Your rights as an investor

      • Ask for the name and registration details of the broker and Authorised Person you are dealing with.
      • Receive complete information on risks, obligations and costs before you invest.
      • Receive advice suited to your financial needs and risk profile.
      • Receive your funds and securities on time, and get a clear statement of your account.
      • Understand the terms and conditions of every transaction.
      • Close your account at any time, and have your remaining funds and securities returned.
      • Raise a complaint and have it considered fairly, and escalate it if you are not satisfied.

      How complaints are handled

      • Step 1 · Fin Venue Ventures / Mirae Asset Sharekhan: write to info@finvenueventures.com or the broker. Complaints are to be resolved within 21 calendar days of receipt.
      • Step 2 · SEBI SCORES: if you are not satisfied, or there is no reply in time, lodge your complaint on SCORES ↗. It is first reviewed by the stock exchange, and you can ask for a second review by SEBI.
      • Step 3 · Online dispute resolution: if the matter is still unresolved, you can start conciliation and arbitration online through SMART ODR ↗.

      Full contact details and the broker's escalation matrix are on our Investor grievance page.

      Do's

      • Read all documents and conditions before signing the account opening form.
      • Get a copy of your KYC and account opening documents, and your Unique Client Code.
      • Register your own mobile number and email, so you get alerts from the exchange and depository directly.
      • Check every contract note and statement, and report any mismatch immediately.
      • Pay margins only by banking channels, to the broker's designated bank account, never in cash.
      • Check that the broker and Authorised Person are registered, on the exchange and SEBI websites.

      Don'ts

      • Don't deal with unregistered brokers or entities.
      • Don't leave any field blank in forms you sign.
      • Don't share your trading password, PIN or OTP with anyone, including us.
      • Don't transfer money to anyone other than your stock broker.
      • Don't fall for schemes that promise guaranteed or assured returns.
      • Don't follow tips on social media, SMS or chat groups without checking them.

      Your responsibilities

      • Give complete and correct KYC information, and keep it up to date.
      • Keep your mobile number, email and bank details current with your broker.
      • Review your contract notes, statements and the depository's Consolidated Account Statement (CAS).
      • Understand the product and its risks before you invest, and invest according to your own risk appetite.

      LearnFAQ
      Home/Learn

      Learn the markets

      Short, plain-language guides to investing, trading and staying safe, plus an A to Z glossary.

      Getting startedMutual fundsTrading and IPOsStaying safeGlossary

      Getting started

      Demat vs trading account

      A trading account is used to place buy and sell orders on the exchange (NSE or BSE). A demat account holds your shares, ETFs and bonds in electronic form with a depository (CDSL or NSDL). You need both, linked to your bank account. When you open an account through us, Mirae Asset Sharekhan opens all of them together.

      How a share trade works

      You place an order, the exchange matches it with a seller, and you get a contract note by email the same day. Indian equity markets settle on T+1: shares reach the buyer's demat account, and money reaches the seller, on the next working day.

      Delivery means you buy and hold the shares. Intraday means you buy and sell on the same day; it is faster-moving and riskier.

      Before you invest: the basics
      • Keep an emergency fund of 3–6 months' expenses in a safe place first.
      • Get adequate life and health insurance.
      • Clear high-interest loans such as credit-card debt.
      • Then invest regularly, for clear goals, with a time horizon in mind.

      Mutual funds

      SIP or lump sum?

      A SIP invests a fixed amount every month. You buy more units when prices are low and fewer when they are high (rupee-cost averaging), and it builds a habit. A lump sum invests a larger amount at once and suits a long horizon when you already have the money. If you have a large amount but are worried about timing, a Systematic Transfer Plan (STP) can move it into equity gradually. Neither method guarantees returns.

      Try the SIP calculator →

      Types of mutual funds
      • Equity funds invest mainly in shares. Higher potential returns, higher ups and downs; best for 5+ years.
      • Debt funds invest in bonds and money-market instruments. Steadier, for shorter goals.
      • Hybrid funds mix equity and debt.
      • Index funds and ETFs track an index such as the Nifty 50, at low cost.
      • ELSS is an equity fund with a 3-year lock-in and a tax deduction under the old tax regime.
      What is NAV?

      Net Asset Value is the price of one unit of a mutual fund, calculated at the end of each business day. A low NAV does not make a fund "cheap"; what matters is how the fund's investments grow.

      Trading and IPOs

      Futures and options (F&O), explained

      F&O are derivatives: contracts whose value depends on a share or index. They are traded in fixed lot sizes and need margin, which means small price moves can create large gains or losses. An option buyer can lose the full premium paid; futures and option sellers can lose much more than their margin.

      A SEBI study found that 9 out of 10 individual F&O traders made net losses. F&O is generally not suitable for first-time investors. Read the risk disclosure →

      How to apply for an IPO
      1. You need a demat account and a UPI ID.
      2. Apply for the number of lots you want within the price band, while the issue is open.
      3. Approve the UPI mandate on your phone. The money is blocked in your bank, not debited.
      4. If you get an allotment, the amount is debited and shares are credited before listing. Otherwise the block is released.
      5. Shares usually list on the exchange within 3 working days of the issue closing.

      See current IPOs →

      Stop-loss and position size

      A stop-loss is an order that exits a position automatically if the price falls to a level you choose, so one bad trade does not wipe out your capital. Many traders also limit how much of their capital they risk on any single trade.

      Staying safe

      Protect your account
      • Never share your password, PIN or OTP with anyone, including us.
      • Keep your own mobile number and email registered, and read the exchange and depository alerts you receive.
      • Check your contract notes and the monthly Consolidated Account Statement (CAS) from CDSL or NSDL.
      • Pay only into your broker's designated bank account.
      Spotting investment frauds
      • Be wary of anyone promising guaranteed or "fixed" returns from the stock market.
      • Avoid "tips" from social-media groups, unknown callers or fake apps that copy well-known brands.
      • Check registration of any broker or advisor on the SEBI website before you deal with them.

      Something doesn't look right? Contact us.

      A to Z

      Market glossary

      Plain-language meanings of terms you will hear from us and in the markets.

      AMC
      Asset Management Company, the company that runs a mutual fund.
      ASBA
      Application Supported by Blocked Amount: your IPO money stays in your bank, blocked, until allotment.
      Bear market
      A period when prices fall broadly and confidence is low.
      Bull market
      A period when prices rise broadly and confidence is high.
      CAS
      Consolidated Account Statement: a monthly statement of all your demat holdings and mutual funds.
      Circuit limit
      The maximum a share can rise or fall in a day before trading in it is paused.
      Contract note
      The legal record of every trade you make, sent by your broker within 24 hours.
      Delivery trade
      Buying shares to hold them in your demat account beyond the same day.
      Depository Participant (DP)
      The agent of CDSL or NSDL that maintains your demat account, here Mirae Asset Sharekhan.
      Dividend
      A share of a company's profit paid to its shareholders.
      ELSS
      Equity Linked Savings Scheme: a tax-saving equity mutual fund with a 3-year lock-in.
      ETF
      Exchange-Traded Fund: a fund that tracks an index or asset and trades like a share.
      Expiry
      The date on which a futures or options contract ends.
      Index
      A basket of shares that represents the market or a sector, such as the Nifty 50 or Sensex.
      Intraday
      Buying and selling the same share on the same trading day.
      KYC
      Know Your Customer: the one-time identity and address verification needed to invest.
      Large / mid / small cap
      Companies grouped by size (market capitalisation). Smaller companies tend to be more volatile.
      Lot size
      The fixed number of shares or units in one F&O contract or IPO application.
      Margin
      The money you must keep with your broker to take a trade, especially in F&O.
      Market capitalisation
      A company's share price multiplied by its total number of shares.
      NAV
      Net Asset Value: the price of one mutual fund unit, set at the end of each business day.
      Nifty 50
      NSE's index of 50 large companies across sectors.
      Nominee
      The person who receives your investments if something happens to you.
      P/E ratio
      Price-to-earnings: a share's price divided by its earnings per share, a common valuation measure.
      Portfolio
      All the investments you hold together.
      Price band
      The range within which an IPO is priced, or within which a share can trade on a day.
      Sensex
      BSE's index of 30 large, well-established companies.
      SIP
      Systematic Investment Plan: investing a fixed amount at regular intervals.
      Stop-loss
      An order that sells automatically if the price falls to a level you choose.
      STP
      Systematic Transfer Plan: moving money gradually from one fund to another.
      STT
      Securities Transaction Tax, charged on buying and selling shares and derivatives.
      SWP
      Systematic Withdrawal Plan: taking a fixed amount out of a fund at regular intervals.
      T+1 settlement
      Trades are settled on the next working day after the trade date.
      Volatility
      How much and how quickly a price moves up and down.
      XIRR
      A return measure that accounts for investments made on different dates, as in a SIP.

      No matching term. Ask us on WhatsApp →

      Frequently asked questions

      Quick answers about accounts, charges, investments, insurance and support.

      Account & charges

      Is opening a demat account free?

      No fees for account opening, advisory or portfolio reviews, for life. Brokerage, annual maintenance and statutory charges apply as per Mirae Asset Sharekhan's tariff. We explain every charge before you open your account.

      Is your advisory free?

      Yes. Our guidance, free consultation and portfolio review carry no advisory fee and no obligation to invest.

      How do I open an account?

      Click "Open Free Demat Account" to apply online on Mirae Asset Sharekhan's secure portal, with Fin Venue Ventures Private Limited as your Authorised Person. It usually takes about 15 minutes.

      What documents do I need?

      PAN, Aadhaar with a linked mobile number, bank proof (cancelled cheque or statement), your signature and a photo. Income proof is needed only for F&O.

      Where are my shares and money held?

      Your shares are held in your own demat account with a SEBI-registered depository, and trades are executed through Mirae Asset Sharekhan on NSE and BSE. Always pay only into your broker's designated bank account.

      Investments

      Which products do you offer?

      Equity and F&O trading, mutual funds and SIPs, PMS, our in-house Investiger strategy, AIFs, unlisted shares, bonds, insurance and tax planning.

      How much do I need to start a SIP?

      Many mutual funds allow SIPs from a small monthly amount. Tell us your goal and we will suggest an amount and the right schemes for you.

      Can you help me apply for IPOs?

      Yes. We track current and upcoming IPOs and help you apply through your demat account using a UPI mandate.

      What is Investiger?

      Investiger is our in-house mini-PMS, actively handled by a dedicated fund manager, with a lower entry point than a traditional PMS.

      Do you give stock tips?

      No. We do not share tips. We help you build a plan suited to your goals and risk profile, backed by research.

      Insurance

      Which insurance companies do you work with?

      We offer life and general insurance from HDFC, ICICI and Bajaj: HDFC Life, ICICI Prudential Life and Bajaj Life for life cover, and HDFC ERGO, ICICI Lombard and Bajaj General for health, motor, home and travel.

      Will you help me at claim time?

      Yes. We help you with the paperwork and follow up with the insurer until your claim is settled.

      Contact & support

      When can I reach you?

      Our office at 132, Neo Corporate Plaza, Malad West, Mumbai is open Monday to Saturday, 8:30 AM to 6:30 PM. Call +91 93244 99656, or email info@finvenueventures.com.

      How do I raise a complaint?

      Write to info@finvenueventures.com. If it is not resolved, you can escalate to Mirae Asset Sharekhan and then to SEBI SCORES. See our Investor grievance page for details.
